title: How fast charging works without cooking your battery
description: Fast charging is more power plus a negotiation between charger and phone. Here's how it works and why it slows near the end.

scenes.say: Fast charging isn't magic. It's more power, plus a quick negotiation before any of it flows.
Power is voltage multiplied by current. Nine volts at three amps is twenty-seven watts. Raise either one, and the battery fills faster, as long as it can take it.
When you plug in, the charger and phone talk first. The charger lists what it can offer. The phone picks what its battery can safely handle. That's how standards like USB Power Delivery work.
Charging has two phases. Fast charging mainly exploits the first, constant current. Then the current tapers off. That's why the last stretch past about eighty percent feels slow.
Some phones split current across two cells. But Battery University says high currents shorten battery life, and heat adds to it. Phones also slow charging themselves when hot. Follow for more.
